basics.name: Aidan McLean
basics.label: Full-Stack Developer
basics.status: Research Assistant @ McMaster Faculty of Engineering
basics.lede: I build systems end to end — the schema, the API, the interface on top of it, and the server it runs on. Right now that's a research platform at McMaster where teams benchmark AI battery models against one another.
basics.contactNote: Open to hearing about backend, full-stack, and infrastructure work. The fastest way to reach me is email.

highlights: Architected and developed a full-stack research platform (Node.js/Express, TypeScript, React, PostgreSQL) that lets researchers submit and benchmark AI battery State-of-Charge models against one another, ranking submissions across 18+ evaluation metrics.

Delivered features end to end across the stack, from REST API endpoints to the React components consuming them, including model submission workflows, results export, an in-app notification system, and an administrative management console.

Designed the PostgreSQL schema (Drizzle ORM) covering authentication, model metadata, and evaluation history, and implemented cookie-based session authentication, rate limiting, and role-based access control across all protected routes.

Built an asynchronous evaluation pipeline that runs each submission in an isolated Docker container, enabling concurrent scoring of multiple models without cross-submission interference, and delivers results through the notification system and email.

Manage deployment on an Ubuntu server (Compute Canada's OpenStack cloud), including NGINX configuration, PM2 process management, and SSL/TLS certificate renewal; incorporate agentic AI development tools (e.g. Claude Code) into the workflow for debugging, code review, and infrastructure scripting.
Customized Drupal Webforms with JavaScript to implement dynamic form behaviour, validation, and improved user experience.
Built front-end integrations with Microsoft APIM to apply business logic, route requests securely, and connect forms to backend services.
Developed a TypeScript front-end application that integrated with an internal GIS map server to retrieve and visualize location-based data.
Picked up Drupal, APIM, and Power Automate on the job and put them straight to use on live production forms.
Documented APIs, workflows, and form logic so other developers could pick up the work without re-deriving it.

projects.name: Record Label E-Commerce Platform
projects.summary: A production storefront, admin console, and in-person point-of-sale for an independent record label: dual-currency pricing, idempotent order processing, role-gated administration, and analytics that refuse to lie.
projects.detail: A TypeScript monorepo on Turborepo and pnpm workspaces — two Next.js 16 / React 19 applications over four shared internal packages, around 35K lines against 36 Postgres tables and 24 versioned migrations. The organizing constraint is currency: the label prices records per currency rather than converting, so USD and CAD are independent columns resolved through a three-level chain, and almost every subsystem downstream has to stay honest about which currency it is talking about.
highlights: Caught a class of silent pricing bug where SQL min() ignores NULLs and produced plausible but unbuyable prices; closed it with a bool_and completeness guard enforced in both the query layer and the admin form.

Built zero-CLS currency switching that preserves Incremental Static Regeneration — both prices are dual-rendered server-side and one is selected by a pre-paint inline script plus CSS, so product pages stay statically generated while serving per-visitor currency.

Made Stripe Checkout idempotent end to end: signature-verified webhooks, a reconciliation cron as a backstop for lost events, and inventory reserved at session creation with automatic sweeping of abandoned checkouts.

Built a channel- and currency-aware analytics layer that refuses to sum across currencies, pins a deterministic default so figures never silently change between page loads, and labels excluded orders rather than reporting a partial number as a total.

Shipped a mobile-first point-of-sale for live shows: offline-style cash and e-transfer sales, oversell-tolerant stock decrements through an inventory ledger, per-currency line re-pricing, and cost snapshots taken in the sale's own currency so margin stays accurate.

Enforced role-based access control on better-auth with granular permission statements across three roles, checked on every admin route and server action and backed by an append-only audit log on all money, inventory, and user mutations.

Hardened every public trust boundary: Zod validation before any database access, IP-keyed rate limiting on unauthenticated endpoints, honeypot bot filtering, parameterized queries, CSP headers, and generic client errors with server-side-only detail.

Established the release workflow after a schema-lag outage: migration-first deploy sequencing, GitHub Actions applying migrations to Neon on merge, and a typecheck, lint, test, and build gate across all 16 workspace tasks.

projects.name: SoC Model Benchmarking Platform
projects.summary: A research platform where teams upload AI battery State-of-Charge models and have them scored against a shared benchmark. Submissions are graded on 18+ metrics and ranked against every other entry.
projects.detail: The hard part is isolation: every submission is arbitrary researcher code, so each one runs in its own Docker container through an asynchronous evaluation pipeline. Multiple models score concurrently without interfering with each other, and results come back through an in-app notification system and email. Auth, model metadata, and evaluation history live in a PostgreSQL schema I designed with Drizzle ORM, behind cookie-based sessions, rate limiting, and role-based access control.
